category_zh: 微分方程 / 常微分方程
literal_source_claim_zh: 多项式根的实部为负的条件
literal_source_claim_en: Conditions for the real parts of a polynomial's roots to be negative.
statement_blocker: The catalog does not fix the coefficient domain and ordering, exact-degree and leading-coefficient premises, real-to-complex root encoding, strict half-plane convention, finite Hurwitz matrix orientation and zero extension, leading-principal-minor indices, determinant versus Routh-array formulation, boundary cases, or exact equivalence directions. Inspected sources narrow the classical family but do not replace an independently accepted source/translation/errata crosswalk and binder-complete Lean statement.
domain_and_universes: Open: likely a finite-degree real polynomial, complex roots after scalar extension, and finite real matrices indexed by degree; the source-selected degree carrier, coefficient adapter, and universes are not frozen.
conclusion: Open: the catalog does not yet select an exact iff between strict left-half-plane roots and a precisely indexed finite Hurwitz-determinant predicate.
degenerate_case_status: No case is silently excluded before the proposition is frozen; n = 0, degree drop, zero or negative leading coefficient, imaginary-axis and repeated roots, zero minors, and scaling/reversal conventions require explicit source-mapped decisions.
candidate_scope_not_credited: for a real degree-n polynomial with positive leading coefficient, every complex root has negative real part if and only if every leading principal determinant of the finite Hurwitz matrix is positive
the equivalent Routh-array sign criterion with all exceptional and zero-row cases specified
an ascending-coefficient or reciprocal-polynomial transport checked against the descending-coefficient finite-matrix theorem
excluded_substitutions: a quadratic, cubic, quartic, or numerical special case
a matrix eigenvalue, linear-system, Lyapunov, discrete-time Schur, or Jury stability theorem
a Routh table, root count, Hermite-Biehler, Lienard-Chipart, or total-positivity theorem without a checked source-mapped transport
Holtz's ascending-coefficient infinite-matrix factorization used as though it were definitionally the finite descending-coefficient theorem
a complex-coefficient generalization or a closed-left-half-plane/nonnegative-minor weakening
generic root, real-part, matrix, submatrix, and determinant APIs treated as a target theorem
a definition, structure field, or premise that assumes the desired equivalence
the catalog's untrusted verified label, source discovery, or API probe treated as proof credit
